fieldValues.title: At most one copy of a repository per boundary
fieldValues.decision_rationale: Splitting work off is a slice, which already mints a new id and records its origin. Two repositories sharing an id are clones or worktrees: the same repository at another version, which a re-id rule would mis-model as a different repository.
fieldValues.decision_statement: A clone keeps its source's `repositoryId`, so only one of them can be a boundary member; no re-id rule is added.
fieldValues.decision_scope: Copies of one repository in a boundary: at most one, because a clone keeps its repositoryId; no re-id rule.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: A re-id rule giving a diverged copy a new id (mis-models a worktree, which is the same repository at another version).
fieldValues.accepted_costs: Listing a worktree and its main checkout in one registry makes both entries fail ([R4]), so neither is reachable; if one is the default, the implementation reports that its default has no usable entry. Each needs its own registry or process.
evidence_refs: srs-programme conversation container ec40e5ab (the owner's words, 2026-10-30 to 2026-11-02)
fieldValues.review_trigger:
1. The owner or an agent regularly needs a worktree and its main checkout in one session. *Checked at:* srs-rust#683's first use with worktrees (`scripts/wt`), and any friction finding filed against it.
2. Forks that diverge but are not slices need to coexist with their source in one boundary. *Checked at:* the first such fork.
